canonical_statement: For a finite family of jointly independent measurable real random variables on a probability space, if every tilted exponential is integrable, then for every real threshold a and positive real tilt t, the real-valued probability that their sum is at least a is at most exp(-t*a) times the product of their tilted exponential integrals.
domain_and_universes: universes u v; Omega : Type u with a measurable space; probability measure mu; finite index type I : Type v; X : I -> Omega -> Real; a t : Real; Prop in universe 0
hypotheses: forall i, Integrable (fun omega => Real.exp (t * X i omega)) mu
conclusion: mu.real {omega | a <= sum i, X i omega} <= Real.exp (-t * a) * product i, integral omega, Real.exp (t * X i omega) dmu
